To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the slowpoke C2/C3 regulatory region has important roles in regulating developmental expression in both CNS neurons and adult muscle and eye-specific expression.
a region downstream from the slowpoke Ca(+)2-activated K(+) channel gene's coding sequence contains elements that regulate developmental- and eye-specific expression.

a downstream intron of the slowpoke gene contains eye- and muscle-specific transcription control elements that regulate developmental expression of slowpoke in both the central nervous system and musculature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the nervous system develops and functions and we are interested in the role of ion channels in these processes.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the regulation of ion channels in the nervous system.
understanding the mechanisms that determine when and where a gene is turned on.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this region is an important modulator of slowpoke expression in both the nervous and musculature systems.
the C2-C3 region contains both positive and negative regulatory elements which control the expression of slowpoke in a tissue- and developmental-specific fashion.
this intronic region contains a number of elements that can regulate slowpoke expression both in the CNS and in the eye and that these elements are developmentally regulated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this intronic region contains elements that are necessary and sufficient to activate the slowpoke promoter in the eye, and that these elements are also sufficient to activate a basal promoter in adult muscle, but are not necessary to maintain adult muscle expression.
the C2C3 region contains elements that can activate transcription in the CNS and muscle and eye, but that these elements are developmentally regulated.
the C2C3 region contains both positive and negative regulatory elements that are active in the CNS and muscle during development and in the eye during adult development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
introns are not just spacers between exons but can contain regulatory elements that can be utilized to modulate gene expression.
a single intronic region can contain elements that regulate expression of the same gene in different tissues and at different stages of development.
intronic regions can contain elements that can modulate transcriptional control of the gene they reside within and that this can be developmentally regulated.
